source.title: Predator–Prey Model: Driven Hunt for Accelerated Grokking
source.authors: I. A. Lopatin; S. Kozyrev; A. N. Pechen

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some equations, table formatting, and figure text are flattened or garbled, but the paper's text and captions describe the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The study explicitly reproduces known grokking results using AdamW on modular arithmetic and MNIST, then tests additional optimization methods and grokking-time dependencies.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports results on Rosenbrock optimization, optimizer comparisons, ablations, and curriculum learning. These are included only where they report grokking behavior or timing; unrelated optimization results and background claims cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The main contribution is a new optimizer (PPM). Its own results still bear on the claim: Section 2 reproduces AdamW grokking on modular division mod 97 and the Omnigrok MNIST setup. Section 5 measures grokking time against training-set fraction and against initial weight norm with plain AdamW. These bear on V1 and on V3's data and initialization parts. The PPM, PPM-conn and optimizer-comparison results report method performance only.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that PPM and PPM-conn accelerate grokking on modular arithmetic and MNIST by up to about 100× in gradient calls and about 60× in wall-clock time. They frame grokking as slow motion along a ravine, and the method as possibly worse on landscapes without ravines. They describe the exponential dependence of AdamW grokking time on sample size, and its linear dependence on initial weight norm, as 'proven'; in fact both are numerical fits.
record.recipe_differences: The study reproduces grokking with AdamW on modular division and MNIST, but its modular task is division modulo 97 rather than the original modular-addition example; it also uses a separate modular-addition setup modulo 139 for the sample-size and initialization sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking time varies with training sample fraction and initial weight norm. PPM-conn results vary with its interaction parameters; the paper reports ablations over σ, A, and αp.

fits_no_version.finding: A predator–prey coupled-replica optimizer applied after memorization reaches the generalization threshold about 20–100× faster in gradient calls than AdamW. Linear curriculum learning roughly halves wall-clock grokking time on modular division.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The grokking delay reflects slow motion along a flat ravine and can be shortened greatly by optimizers that drive motion along it.

fits_no_version.finding: In Table 3, several optimizers reach the test threshold in roughly 10³–10⁴ epochs. RMSprop and SGD with default settings, and some NAdam, RAdam and Lion settings, do not reach it within a 10⁴-epoch budget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Time to grok depends strongly on the choice of optimizer and its hyperparameters.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Artificial Intelligence (stated venue)
record.problems: Some grokking trajectories and the Figure 6 scaling curves are reported only in plots, without exact point values in the text. Table 3 averages only five runs, and the paper notes that grokking time varies across launches and seeds. The provided text contains occasional flattened or garbled formatting.
record.rows_left_out: None. The row set is below the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Only modular division and modular addition are tested. Test accuracy starting from chance is not quantified. The sample-size sweep covers a single prime and architecture.
Text and molecule data are not tested. Switching grokking on or off through initialization or weight norm is not shown, and no lazy-to-rich transition is examined.
Not tested; no circuit or progress-measure analysis.
Not tested; no critical dataset size or ungrokking.
Not tested. The optimizer comparison does not isolate instabilities or floating-point effects.

missing.what: Baseline AdamW time to grok stated in text: about 4×10³ epochs for ModuloOperation and about 8×10³ for MNIST. The text also says this time depends strongly on initialization.
With PPM-conn, no explicit dependence of grokking iterations on sample size could be found.

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a method paper; most rows are method performance and are relinked to none. The V3 support rests on the Omnigrok MNIST recipe, which scales up initial weights. The study does not identify itself as a source of either original. Grokking-time estimates use few runs: 3 per point in Fig. 6 and 5 per cell in Table 3.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests modular arithmetic and MNIST, but not every algorithmic dataset or a systematic range of training-set sizes using the original grokking setup.
It does not identify or track a Fourier/generalizing circuit, memorizing components, or continuous circuit-progress measures.

It tests MNIST and reports a relation between initial weight norm and grokking time, but does not test text or molecule data, a lazy-to-rich transition, or switching grokking fully on and off through initialization.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested.
The paper studies grokking time versus sample size, but does not test the low-norm efficiency account, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below such a size.
The study does not compare learned algorithms across runs.
It does not test adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifacts as explanations for grokking.

rows.measure: Training and test accuracy trajectory
rows.note: The text describes delayed test-accuracy increase after training accuracy rises. The MNIST setup uses MSE, no output softmax, and a 1,000-image subsample.

rows.subject: Decoder-Only Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Varied the training sample fraction and measured epochs to grok
rows.measure: Grokking time versus training sample fraction
rows.value: figure only; text gives Tg ∼ B e^(−β/η)
rows.note: The paper says grokking time decreases exponentially as sample size grows; each plotted point is based on a random subsample. Exact point values are not given in the text.
rows.check: Log epochs to grok fall linearly with sample fraction β (Fig. 6 left), so the delay grows as the data shrink. The setup is modular addition mod 139 with a 95% test threshold, a smaller model and embedding std 0.02. The text calls the law 'proven', but it is a numerical fit.

relationships.condition: AdamW, transformer on modular division mod 97 and modular addition mod 139
relationships.reason: Test accuracy rises well after train accuracy saturates (~4×10³ epochs, R1). Log grokking time falls linearly as the training fraction grows (R3).
relationships.display_finding: Test accuracy rose well after training saturation around 4,000 epochs, and logarithmic grokking time decreased linearly as the training fraction increased.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: AdamW baselines on modular division and MNIST, and modular-addition sample-size sweep
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports delayed test-accuracy rise after rapid training accuracy increase, and longer grokking times for smaller sample fractions (R1–R3).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: PPM and PPM-conn on modular division and MNIST
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports grokking under both methods with reported acceleration relative to AdamW (R5–R10).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Some tested optimizer settings did not reach the test-accuracy threshold within 10⁴ epochs, while others did grok (R12, R14, R16–R17, R20, R22–R24).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports delayed generalization on the non-algorithmic image classification setup (R2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Initial weight norm on modular addition
reader_labels.reason: Initial weight norm is associated with grokking time, but the reported result is a time dependence, not a demonstrated on/off switch or lazy-to-rich transition (R4).
